clue.text: Taken advantage of: made to wear purple and yellow

definitions.meaning: an idiom for being swindled or stitched up, like a fish split and smoked

definitions.text: made to wear purple and yellow
definitions.meaning: purple and yellow are UKIP's party colours, and its supporters are nicknamed kippers, so this is being dressed as one

explanation.surface: Someone complains of being exploited by being forced into a garish outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: UKIP (the UK Independence Party) wore purple and yellow, and its members were called kippers; the British idiom for being thoroughly cheated is to be smoked like a herring.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means swindled or stitched up; the second reading puns on UKIP members being nicknamed after the smoked herring.

clue.text: Fraudulently taking sides spelling misery for Sturgeon's supporters

indicators.note: taking away the sides of the word leaves only its inner letters

explanation.surface: A fraudster switching allegiance brings grief to Nicola Sturgeon's backers.
explanation.walkthrough: Nicola Sturgeon led the Scottish National Party, so 'misery for Sturgeon's supporters' asks for a Scots word for grief: DULE (also spelt dool). Strip FRAU and NTLY from either end of 'Fraudulently'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dule is an old Scots word meaning sorrow or grief, fitting for Scottish nationalists.

clue.text: Group of high-fliers, supported by Left, like Ed Miliband's speech

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of, and so is held up by, the second

parts.note: NASA, the US space agency, sends astronauts very high indeed

explanation.surface: A joke at the expense of the Labour leader's adenoidal delivery.
explanation.walkthrough: Ed Miliband, Labour leader in 2015, was often mocked for a nasal voice.
explanation.definitionFit: Miliband's voice was widely described as sounding through the nose.

clue.text: Green perhaps appearing in a French strip

indicators.note: one piece shows up inside the other

parts.note: une is the French for a, feminine
Rob Green was an England goalkeeper, so Green may be a Rob

explanation.surface: A Green Party figure turns up in some French striptease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green' looks like the political party in this election puzzle, but it is the footballer Rob Green, England goalkeeper at the 2010 World Cup.
explanation.definitionFit: To unrobe is to take off one's clothes, which is to undress.

clue.text: One's sprayed emulsion over expensive car

indicators.note: letters sprayed about are scattered into a new order

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone has splashed house paint over a luxury vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sprayed' rearranges I (One) with EMULSION; 'over' just links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A limousine is a large luxurious chauffeur-driven motor, costly to buy or hire.

clue.text: Old trade union leader or what 11 has, I hear

indicators.note: says the word that follows is judged by how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: 11 is 'a kipper', taken as one who kips, and a sleeper has a short sleep or nap

explanation.surface: A clue linking a former union boss to the smoked fish of 11.
explanation.walkthrough: Jimmy Knapp led the RMT rail union. 'Kipper' here is a sleeper, one who kips, so what he has is a NAP.
explanation.definitionFit: Jimmy Knapp was general secretary of the rail workers' union RMT until his death in 2001.

clue.text: Vicious party leader's sort of accompaniment — Greens, perhaps

parts.note: Sid Vicious was the Sex Pistols' bassist
Ed Miliband led the Labour Party; the 's is a link
ish is the casual suffix for more or less

explanation.surface: A nasty politician's style of musical backing, possibly the Green Party.
explanation.walkthrough: Greens look like the Green Party but are leafy vegetables, an example of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish of vegetables served with a main course is a typical extra on the plate.

clue.text: Drip involved in likely election outcome not showing any emotion

indicators.note: one piece is wrapped up inside the other

parts.note: a hung parliament was widely predicted in 2015, a deadlock
IV, intravenous, is a hospital drip

explanation.surface: A political wet is caught up in a hung parliament and stays poker-faced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drip' looks like an insult for a weak politician; it is a hospital IV.
explanation.definitionFit: Impassive means expressionless, showing no feeling.

clue.text: River running through the Bronx

indicators.note: the answer runs across the letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A waterway flowing through the New York borough.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bronx River is real, which makes the surface plausible; the answer is the Spanish river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ebro is a major river of north-east Spain.

clue.text: Like teacher concealing two notes

indicators.note: one piece hides the other inside it

parts.note: pupils address a male teacher as sir
mi and la are notes of the sol-fa scale
mi and la are notes of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A schoolmaster hides a couple of notes, perhaps passed in class.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a teacher confiscating notes; they are musical sol-fa notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Similar means alike, resembling one another.

clue.text: Five years of sexual desire and booze

parts.note: lust is strong sexual desire
rum is a spirit, one kind of booze

explanation.surface: Half a decade of sex and drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A lustrum is a period of half a decade, from the Roman census purification.

clue.text: See 1
What may be experienced towards end of term with the Eds, as Cameron sees them

definitions.text: What may be experienced towards end of term
definitions.meaning: contractions felt at the end of a pregnancy's full term

definitions.text: the Eds, as Cameron sees them
definitions.meaning: Ed Miliband and Ed Balls led Labour, and to Tory David Cameron they were a nuisance from that party

explanation.surface: A Westminster joke about the Labour duo as the Prime Minister's headache at the end of a parliamentary session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'term' looks like the parliamentary term but means a pregnancy's term.
explanation.definitionFit: Childbirth contractions come at the end of pregnancy; the political sense makes the two Eds the Prime Minister's Labour troubles.

clue.text: What might be worn by Scottish 23s or Welsh 23s shortly ()

definitions.text: What might be worn by Scottish 23s
definitions.meaning: 23 is nationalists; a tartan cloth is worn in Scotland
... Cymru is the Welsh nationalist party, its name often cut to its first word

explanation.surface: A note on what Scottish and Welsh separatists wear.
explanation.definitionFit: A tartan cloak or cloth is traditional Highland dress; the Welsh party Plaid Cymru is known by its short name.

clue.text: What politicians often play on: loud organs ()

parts.note: f, forte, is the musical direction for loud
ears are the organs of hearing

explanation.surface: Campaigners exploit them, and they are loud organs too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organs' suggests musical instruments that are played, but means body parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Politicians often exploit voters' anxieties to win support.

clue.text: A regular correction apparently included when listener is on line

indicators.note: in an across clue a piece that is on another comes after it
one piece is taken in by the other

parts.note: a ley or ley line is an alignment of ancient sites
app. is a dictionary abbreviation of apparent or apparently
the ear is the organ that listens

explanation.surface: A periodic adjustment slipped in while someone listens on the phone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apparently' gives AP, the dictionary abbreviation, set inside LEY; 'is on' places EAR after. 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Every four years an extra day in February keeps the calendar in step with the solar year.

clue.text: When the polls close observe leader of DUP rising and they're there

parts.note: UK polling stations close at ten in the evening

indicators.note: in a down clue the pieces read upwards, backwards

parts.note: to see is to observe

indicators.note: takes the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Election night: watch the Democratic Unionist Party chief arrive at the count.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns SEE plus D (leader of DUP) upwards to give DEES. The DUP is Northern Ireland's Democratic Unionist Party.
explanation.definitionFit: People who attend are by definition present at the event.

clue.text: Make more enlightened sign about last of Conservative lies disseminated

indicators.note: one piece goes round the other

parts.note: Libra is a sign of the zodiac

indicators.note: takes the final letter of the word
scattered widely, so the letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A protest placard deals with Tory falsehoods being spread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sign' looks like a placard; it is the star sign. 'disseminated' rearranges LIES into LISE.
explanation.definitionFit: To liberalise is to make laws or attitudes freer and more tolerant.

clue.text: The first female tennis player from Australia from that time

parts.note: Eve was the first woman in Genesis
Pat Rafter was an Australian tennis champion

explanation.surface: The first woman to play top tennis from Down Under.
explanation.walkthrough: Pat Rafter won the US Open twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Ever after means for all time following a point, as in fairy tales.

clue.text: Sort of vote in favour of experiment

parts.note: pro means for
a test is a trial or experiment

explanation.surface: A ballot backing a trial run.
explanation.definitionFit: A protest vote is cast against the main parties rather than for a winner.

clue.text: Took action to somehow reinvent party leader

indicators.note: done somehow, in some undetermined way, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: Ed Miliband led the Labour Party

explanation.surface: A party chief stepped in to remake his leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges REINVENT into INTERVEN; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To intervene is to step in and act in a situation.

clue.text: See 15
Very good dark places in which to see birds

parts.note: pi, short for pious, means very good in crosswords
pits such as mines are dark

explanation.surface: Excellent gloomy hollows where birdwatchers can spot their quarry.
explanation.walkthrough: PI for pious, very good morally, is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Pipits are small songbirds such as the meadow pipit.

clue.text: Politician putting race first

parts.note: a nation is a people or race
the A-list is the top, first-rate group

explanation.surface: A politician who puts his own people above all else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting' is a link; the surface describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: One who campaigns for national independence, such as an SNP member, is a kind of politician.

clue.text: Perhaps Iris or Judith works in the Colosseum ()

definitions.meaning: Iris by Mascagni and Judith by Serov are stage works sung throughout
in Latin, the language of Rome's amphitheatre, opus has the plural form meaning works

explanation.surface: Women's names performed in a Roman arena.
explanation.definitionFit: Iris and Judith are musical dramas; in Latin the word is simply the plural of opus, works.

clue.text: Troubled retailer appearing in magistrates' court ()

indicators.note: the answer shows up within the letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A struggling shop chain is up before the bench.
explanation.walkthrough: Tesco, Britain's biggest supermarket chain, was in trouble in 2015 after an accounting scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: Tesco, the British supermarket giant, had a profits crisis then.

clue.text: See 27

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held is 'See 27': GOOD is the second half of VERY GOOD (27,26), annotated on 27-down, but the puzzle file does not group the two lights, so it cannot be null as a group member.

clue.text: OK, or excellent

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase can mean acceptable, as an acknowledgement, or of high quality.

clue.text: Supervise writing of poetry in Old English

indicators.note: one piece is put within the other

parts.note: verse is writing in poetic form

explanation.surface: A request to write poems in Anglo-Saxon.
explanation.definitionFit: To oversee is to watch over and direct work.

clue.text: The French are in well-trodden Italian city

indicators.note: one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: trite means hackneyed, worn by overuse
es is French for (you) are, as in tu es

explanation.surface: French speakers on a familiar route to an Italian port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The French' wants to be LE or LES; it is 'The French are', French for are.
explanation.definitionFit: Trieste is a port city in north-east Italy.

clue.text: See 6
Just Conservative concealing conclusions from party conferences in improbable account

indicators.note: one piece hides the other within

parts.note: fair means just
a Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party

indicators.note: takes the final letter of each word

explanation.surface: A fair-minded Tory hides what party gatherings decided in a far-fetched tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conclusions' suggests decisions reached at party conferences, but it asks for the final letters of 'party' and 'conferences'.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairy story is a fanciful tale, so any unbelievable explanation.
